clue.text: Initially see little fellow working for a very small amount

indicators.note: Initially says to take only the opening letter of the word see

parts.note: a midge is informally a very small person
on means operating or working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A tiny man is put to work for next to no pay, as you will first notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount or a trace of something is a familiar variant spelling of smidgen.

clue.text: Wonderful boy in charge, travelling very fast

parts.note: super means wonderful
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A great lad in command is racing along.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving faster than sound is travelling extremely fast.

clue.text: Explain being angry about sovereign's desire

indicators.note: about says the word for angry goes around the coin and the desire

parts.note: irate means angry
a sovereign is a gold pound coin, and L is the pound sign
lust is strong desire

explanation.surface: Explain why someone is cross over the monarch's wishes.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is an old British one-pound gold coin, giving L for pound; 'being' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something clear with examples is to explain it.

clue.text: Device for soldier's way of working

parts.note: GI is an American soldier, and with the possessive s gives GIS
MO, modus operandi, is a way of working

explanation.surface: A gadget that suits how a soldier operates.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadget or contraption of any sort is a device.

clue.text: Traveller's joy seeing damn bad loser upset

indicators.note: upset says the letters of damn bad loser are knocked over into another order

explanation.surface: A traveller enjoys watching a sore loser get annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traveller's joy' reads as a tourist's pleasure, but it is a plant name.
explanation.definitionFit: Traveller's joy is the wild clematis, whose fluffy grey seed heads give it its other common name.

clue.text: Recall breaking into storeroom

indicators.note: breaking says the letters of the word recall are smashed and put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone remembers breaking into a store cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recall' looks like a verb in the surface; here it is just the six letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground room used for storing wine, coal or provisions is a storeroom.

clue.text: Development in old conflict

parts.note: ex means former or old
tension is strain or conflict

explanation.surface: A new development in a longstanding dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: An addition built onto a house, or an enlargement, is a development of it.

clue.text: Barren meadow needs a bit of nitrate

parts.note: a lea is a meadow, in poetic use

indicators.note: a bit of says only the first letter of the word nitrate is used

explanation.surface: An unproductive field needs some fertiliser.
explanation.definitionFit: Lean years or lean land yield little, so the word can mean barren or unfruitful.

clue.text: Trick queen over exploit

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the queen above the exploit

parts.note: R is short for regina, queen
to use is to exploit

explanation.surface: A trick to take advantage of the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A cunning ploy or stratagem is a trick.

clue.text: Muslim unhappy in gym for fencing

indicators.note: in places the Muslim name and the word for unhappy inside the school gym lesson

parts.note: PE, physical education, is the school gym lesson
Ali is a common Muslim name
sad means unhappy

explanation.surface: A sad Muslim pupil in a gym lesson is put on fencing.
explanation.walkthrough: PE (physical education) is the British school name for gym class.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence of pointed wooden stakes is a stockade, so it is a kind of fencing.

clue.text: Cooks for the crew aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard puts the crew inside the abbreviation for a ship, as people on board are inside it

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
a team is a crew working together

explanation.surface: A ship's galley staff do the cooking for the sailors on board.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook food by steam is to steam it, so cooks in this way is a third-person verb.

clue.text: Fail to understand girl has article on train

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the article above the word for train

parts.note: a miss is a girl
the is the definite article
to point a weapon is to train or aim it

explanation.surface: A girl with an item on the railway cannot grasp something.
explanation.definitionFit: Not grasping the main idea of something is failing to understand it.

clue.text: Discontinue speech for refreshment

parts.note: to rest is to stop or pause, discontinuing activity
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: Someone cuts a speech short so everyone can get a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Restoring strength or spirits is refreshing them, so the act of restoring is refreshment.

clue.text: Question son's disguise in sleazy bar

indicators.note: in places son and disguise inside the sleazy bar

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable bar
S is the abbreviation for son, with the 's meaning has
to belie is to misrepresent or disguise

explanation.surface: Doubts about a son wearing a disguise in a seedy drinking den.
explanation.definitionFit: To doubt or refuse to accept something as true is to question it.

clue.text: Stop and notice people getting tons of affection

parts.note: an end is a stop
ear means attention or notice, as in give ear
men are people

explanation.surface: Halt and observe people being showered with love.
explanation.definitionFit: A fond word or gesture is an expression of affection.

clue.text: Some dog rescuers become monsters

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Animal rescue workers turn into brutes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'become monsters': the hidden word works as a verb meaning turn into monsters, a whimsical coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are man-eating giants of folk tale, so a verb form fits turning into such brutes.

clue.text: Left USSR wrongly supporting Soviet leader? That's worrying!

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue puts the shuffled letters underneath, holding up the first piece
leader says only the first letter of the word Soviet is used
wrongly says the letters of left USSR are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Abandoning the USSR in the wrong way, while backing a Soviet boss, is nerve-racking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' is fodder, not L: LEFT plus USSR rearranges to TRESSFUL, which goes under the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Something causing anxiety and strain is worrying.

clue.text: American photo taken in Israel produces scepticism

indicators.note: taken in puts the American and the photo inside the old name for Israel

parts.note: Sion is a variant spelling of Zion, a name for Israel
pic is short for picture or photo

explanation.surface: A US snapshot shot in Israel makes people doubt it.
explanation.walkthrough: SION, the alternative spelling of Zion, stands for Israel here.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubt or mistrust about something's truth is both scepticism and suspicion.

clue.text: The miners adapted to join closely together

indicators.note: adapted says the letters of the miners are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Pit workers adjusted to fit in tightly with one another.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear teeth or networks that interlock are said to mesh with each other, joining tightly.

clue.text: Half-heartedly incapacitate an aristocrat

indicators.note: half-heartedly says one of the two central letters, half of the word's heart, is dropped

parts.note: to nobble is to disable a racehorse, incapacitating it

explanation.surface: Someone half-heartedly tries to put a nobleman out of action.
explanation.walkthrough: NOBBLE, British slang for drugging or disabling a racehorse, has BB at its heart; losing one B halves it.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer or member of the titled class is an aristocrat.

clue.text: Boxing promoter in the waste business?

definitions.text: Boxing promoter in the waste business?

parts.words: Boxing promoter in the waste business?
parts.note: a scrap is a fight, so a boxing promoter might be called a dealer in scraps, which is also a trader in metal waste

explanation.surface: A fight promoter who dabbles in rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrap means both a fight and waste metal, so one who deals in fights is, by the pun, the trader in waste.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant buying and selling discarded metal works in the waste trade.

clue.text: Top swimmer receives ten cents

indicators.note: receives puts ten and cents inside the swimmer

parts.note: an eel is a swimming fish
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A champion swimmer earns a dime.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo or surpass others is to top them.

clue.text: Conflict Mike finds heated

parts.note: war is armed conflict
Mike is M in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: Mike finds a dispute getting heated.
explanation.definitionFit: Heated means warmed, made warmer, so the two are synonyms as adjectives.

clue.text: Penny has fish? I ask you!

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that a penny comes with fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is the old-fashioned interjection, as in 'pray tell'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a polite old interjection it means please or I beg you, an entreaty.

clue.text: Disagreement following publicity that's aimless

indicators.note: following says the disagreement comes after the publicity

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, publicity
a rift is a split or disagreement

explanation.surface: A quarrel follows a pointless advertising campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Drifting with no direction or purpose is being without an aim.

clue.text: Man returned to island unattached

indicators.note: returned says the man's name is read backwards

parts.note: Sid is a man's name
Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: A man came back to an island, now single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' tempts as the Isle of Man; it is just a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Separate and distinct things are not joined, so they are unattached.

clue.text: Insect can escape

parts.note: may means is allowed to, can
to fly is to flee or escape

explanation.surface: An insect is able to get away.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-lived winged insect that lives by water is a type of insect.

clue.text: Let's list components? That's most unmoving!

indicators.note: components treats the letters of let's list as parts to be reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: Someone proposes listing the parts of something completely static.
explanation.definitionFit: Still means motionless, so its superlative is the most motionless.
